The manual surfaces — admin_manual entry, owner_manual entry/clear, and the admin-only Correction path (#645)
The §4.3 dispatch gate: a narrow consent+suppression precondition that must never call evaluateAsk (#630, amendments B6 item 4)
Unsubscribe token MINTING at dispatch — this ticket creates the table only (amendments B4)

user_visible_behavior: A batch candidate whose Normalized handle carries a Suppression ledger row is withheld with reason 'suppressed', carrying the ledger's source and suppressed_at verbatim as evidence — the owner sees WHY the list shrank instead of contacts vanishing silently.
A withheld-suppressed candidate does not consume BATCH_CAP (evaluateBatch counts eligible as decision === 'send' only).
The account-offboarding purge receipt email states how many opt-out records are retained so those opt-outs continue to be honored, and lists no addresses.
An account-scoped (owner_manual) suppression row is deleted by the offboarding purge; a global row survives it with account_id intact, pointing at the already-tombstoned accounts row.
invariants: Invariant #14 posture: RLS enabled with zero policies on both new tables — browser/client code never reads or writes them; a direct client read of a global row would expose account_id provenance that §7.4 forbids surfacing.
Invariant #8: every owner-facing read stays scoped by account_id; the §1.2 lookup's account arm is keyed on the caller's account_id and can never match another tenant's row.
Invariant #10: SHA-256 via node:crypto for token_hash; never crypto-js.
Invariant #5: raw unsubscribe tokens exist only in memory and in the sent message — never in Postgres, outbox payloads, or logs. This ticket stores hashes only.
Invariant #15: suppression.ts and every account-offboarding module take sql/tx as an explicit parameter and never import @/lib/db/server.

DR2 — the ledger is solicitation-only: no transactional or notification-email path may consult it, or an owner who opted out as somebody else's customer stops receiving approval emails and reaches invariant #3 sideways.
First-write-wins: ON CONFLICT … DO NOTHING against both partial unique indexes; a later source never overwrites an earlier row.
Both evaluation points are EXISTENCE checks — no comparison is ever made against suppressed_at, deliberately sidestepping the postgres.js microsecond-truncation class.
§4.2 populate, never pre-filter: the shipped, contract-tested precedence-2 'suppressed' gate in evaluateAsk must not become dead code.
Lock order: any new writer of a solicitation table honours acquireCsvIngestLock then acquireSolicitationBatchLock, advisory-before-row, ordered by business.id — or it is an ABBA deadlock.
TABLE_DISPOSITIONS stays alphabetically sorted (table-disposition.test.ts:107) — entries insert in place, never append.
Fail-closed purge verification: a table in the disposition inventory with no verification branch throws missing_purge_verification_sql:<table>, never silently passes.
edge_cases: outreach_id is a PLAIN UUID with a partial UNIQUE index and NO FK. A CASCADE FK would delete the retained token rows on purge (solicitation_outreach cascades from solicitation_batches from contact_csv_uploads — purge-verification.ts:596-599), breaking the post-purge redemption §5.2 exists to guarantee. This matches how §2.2 already treats ask_id. Amendment B9's FK wording predates the retention analysis; recorded as a spec amendment.

solicitation_suppressions carries ONE disposition entry, not the two §6.3's table implies: TABLE_DISPOSITIONS is keyed by table name and verificationQuery is a switch (table), so two entries would hit the same case arm twice. The single allowed_limited_retention arm asserts BOTH facts — no surviving account-scoped rows AND no retained global row still referencing one of the account's users — so the check can actually fail rather than being vacuously green.

Global wins when a handle matches both a global row and this account's own owner_manual row: ORDER BY (scope = 'global') DESC, suppressed_at ASC LIMIT 1. Reporting the account row would let an owner clear it under §7.6, watch the contact stay suppressed, and have no idea why.

Both partial unique indexes lead with (channel, normalized_handle), but the purge delete, the retained-row count and the token scrub all filter account_id-first. PG16 has no skip scan, so 096 ships an account_id-leading index on each table — the migration-095 lesson, applied up front instead of in a review round.
VerifyAccountOffboardingPurgeInput needs NO widening: the account's users are derivable by subquery, exactly as the analytics_events arm already does at purge-verification.ts:351.

The retained-suppression count is taken at finalize time and covers global suppression rows only. Token rows are excluded on the merits — they are pending opt-out mechanisms, not opt-out records — and their account_id is scrubbed by then, so counting them would need extra ordering machinery.
The CHECK pairing is one-directional: scope='account' requires account_id NOT NULL; a global row MAY still carry account_id as provenance.
A second recordSuppression for an already-suppressed handle is a no-op success and must not mint a duplicate analytics event.
solicitation_contacts.email already stores the normalized handle — the consent LEFT JOIN at batch-builder.ts:417-420 proves it — so the suppression lookup joins on c.email with no re-normalization.

recordSuppression has ZERO production callers in this ticket (its consumers are #644/#645/#627). It ships anyway, proven by a live-DB integration suite, because the byte-for-byte ON CONFLICT predicate needs one owner and needs proving at the moment the indexes are created. Expect a fallow unused-export finding requiring a justified suppression.

The suppressed withhold gate goes live but stays dormant in prod: zero rows exist until #644/#645/#627 ship writers. Zero solicitation_suppressed events is the expected steady state, not a failure signal.

Registering solicitation_suppressed_at_dispatch here (emitted by #630) is deliberate: TS-allowlist-only registration rolls back every emitting transaction and ci:analytics-events does not catch it (089's lesson, restated in 094's header). Registering both keeps #644 and #630 migration-free.

rollback_plan: Ordered, and the window closes when the first writer ships. (1) 097 is a strict CHECK superset of 094's list — reverting the deploy leaves the constraint valid and all existing rows passing, exactly as 094's own rollback note states; no down-migration needed. (2) 096 creates two tables with ZERO production writers in this ticket, so while they are empty `DROP TABLE solicitation_unsubscribe_tokens; DROP TABLE solicitation_suppressions;` is safe. Once #644/#645/#627 land writers it is NOT safe — dropping would destroy compliance records — so this rollback is valid only before the first writer merges. (3) Code revert MUST precede any table drop: batch-builder's LATERAL join, the purge-verification arms and the purge-stages scrub all reference the tables, and dropping first turns every batch build and every offboarding purge into a hard error. Revert the app deploy, confirm no traffic, then drop. (4) Migrations apply staging-first and prod at promotion, in lockstep.
observability: Sentry: `account_offboarding_purge_verification_failed:solicitation_suppressions` — fires when an account-scoped row survived the purge, or when a retained global row still names one of the account's users. Its ABSENCE does NOT prove global rows were retained: the verifier counts violations, so a purge that wrongly deleted every global row also reports zero. Retention is proven by the live-DB survival test, never by this signal (corrected in adversarial review round 2, finding 18).
Sentry: `missing_purge_verification_sql:solicitation_suppressions` or `:solicitation_unsubscribe_tokens` — fires if the disposition entry lands without its verification arm (the fail-closed guard).
The purge_receipt email body carries the retained-count sentence; a staging offboarding dry-run rendering it is the end-to-end proof of the §6.3 receipt requirement.
analytics_events rows named `solicitation_suppressed` — expected count is ZERO in prod until #644 ships a writer. A non-zero count before then means an unintended writer exists.
solicitation_asks.evidence carrying `reason: 'suppressed'` with a populated `suppression_source` — the build-time populate seam working end to end; also zero until writers land.

Worker log line from the batch build path must never interpolate a normalized handle (§9.5: createWorkerLogger sanitizes object args, NOT string args) — correlate on the suppression row id or a token_hash prefix instead.
